scenes.headline: Lions and tigers have a special pad in the larynx.
scenes.body: Snow leopards don't. Their vocal folds can't produce the deep, rumbling roar of the other big cats.

scenes.headline: Instead, they chuff.
scenes.body: A soft, puffing greeting, plus growls, hisses and a long yowl during the mating season.

scenes.headline: Fewer than 10,000 adults remain.
scenes.body: Listed as Vulnerable. They live at 3,000–4,500 m across 12 countries, and most people will never see one.

scenes.headline: One sourced wildlife fact, every day.
scenes.body: Share with someone who thought all big cats roar.

caption:
Snow leopards can't roar. Lions, tigers, jaguars and leopards have a pad of fibro-elastic tissue in the larynx that lets them rumble; the snow leopard doesn't, so it chuffs, growls and yowls instead.

The 'ghost of the mountains' lives at 3,000–4,500 m across 12 countries. Fewer than 10,000 mature adults remain (IUCN: Vulnerable).

Sources: Hast (1989) J. Anatomy; IUCN Red List 2017; Snow Leopard Trust. Photos: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 (captive animals, Zoo Karlsruhe); credits on screen.
